Here's a PHP function that validates an email address with a regex and returns a boolean:

```php
<?php

/**
 * Validates an email address using a regular expression.
 *
 * @param string $email The email address to validate.
 * @return bool True if the email is valid, false otherwise.
 */
function isValidEmail(string $email): bool
{
    // Trim surrounding whitespace
    $email = trim($email);

    // Enforce overall length limit (RFC 5321: max 254 characters)
    if ($email === '' || strlen($email) > 254) {
        return false;
    }

    $pattern = '/^
        (?!\.)                              # local part cannot start with a dot
        (?!.*\.\.)                          # no consecutive dots anywhere
        [A-Za-z0-9!#$%&\'*+\/=?^_`{|}~.-]{1,64}  # local part (max 64 chars)
        (?<!\.)                             # local part cannot end with a dot
        @
        (?:
            [A-Za-z0-9]                     # domain label must start with alphanumeric
            (?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?  # label body, cannot end with hyphen
            \.
        )+
        [A-Za-z]{2,63}                      # top-level domain (letters only)
    $/x';

    return preg_match($pattern, $email) === 1;
}
```

### Usage Example

```php
$testEmails = [
    'user@example.com',          // valid
    'first.last@sub.domain.org', // valid
    'user+tag@example.co.uk',    // valid
    'plainaddress',              // invalid - no @
    '@example.com',              // invalid - no local part
    'user@.com',                 // invalid - domain starts with dot
    'user..name@example.com',    // invalid - consecutive dots
    '.user@example.com',         // invalid - starts with dot
    'user@example',              // invalid - no TLD
    'user@-example.com',         // invalid - label starts with hyphen
];

foreach ($testEmails as $email) {
    printf("%-30s => %s\n", $email, isValidEmail($email) ? 'valid' : 'invalid');
}
```

```
user@example.com               => valid
first.last@sub.domain.org      => valid
user+tag@example.co.uk         => valid
plainaddress                   => invalid
@example.com                   => invalid
user@.com                      => invalid
user..name@example.com         => invalid
.user@example.com              => invalid
user@example                   => invalid
user@-example.com              => invalid
```

### How the Regex Works

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `(?!\.)` | Local part can't begin with a dot |
| `(?!.*\.\.)` | Disallows consecutive dots |
| `[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_\`{|}~.-]{1,64}` | Allowed local-part characters, up to 64 chars |
| `(?<!\.)` | Local part can't end with a dot |
| `@` | Literal at-sign |
| `[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?\.` | Domain label: 1–63 chars, no leading/trailing hyphen |
| `[A-Za-z]{2,63}` | TLD of 2–63 letters |
| `x` flag | Allows whitespace and comments in the pattern for readability |

```php

{
```

```php
    $email = trim($email);
```

```php
    // Enforce overall length limit (RFC 5321: max 254 characters)
    if ($email === '' || strlen($email) > 254) {
        return false;
    }

    $pattern = '/^
        (?!\.)                              # local part cannot start with a dot
        (?!.*\.\.)                          # no consecutive dots anywhere
```
```php
        [A-Za-z0-9!#$%&\'*+\/=?^_`{|}~.-]{1,64}  # local part (max 64 chars)
        (?<!\.)                             # local part cannot end with a dot
```

```php
            (?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?  # may contain hyphens, cannot end with one
            \.

        [A-Za-z]{2,63}                      # top-level domain (letters only)
    $/x';
```

```php
$testEmails = [

    'first.last@sub.domain.org', // valid
    'user+tag@example.co.uk',    // valid
    "o'brien@example.ie",        // valid

    '@example.com',              // invalid - no local part
    'user@',                     // invalid - no domain
    'user..name@example.com',    // invalid - consecutive dots
    '.user@example.com',         // invalid - leading dot
    'user.@example.com',         // invalid - trailing dot in local part
    'user@-example.com',         // invalid - domain label starts with hyphen
    'user@example',              // invalid - no TLD
    'user@example.c',            // invalid - TLD too short
```

|------|---------|

```php
<?php

/**
 * Validates an email address using a regular expression.

 */
```
```php
function validateEmail(string $email): bool
{
```
```php
    $pattern = '/^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&\'*+\/=?^_`{|}~-]+'
             . '@'
             . '[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?'
             . '(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)+$/';

    return (bool) preg_match($pattern, $email);
}
```
